findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the step-4 signer-seam patch inventory to include the intermediate delegators `rebar.signing.sign_manifest` and `rebar.signing._sign_manifest_under_lock` (derived via `find_referencing_symbols` on `mint_opcert_record` and `sign_completion_verdict`), so the optional binding parameter is threaded through every hop from `sign_completion_verdict` to `mint_opcert_record`.
evidence: Plan step 4 enumerates: `ensure_opcert_key` … `opcert_principal` … and their callers `mint_opcert_record`/`sign_opcert_manifest` … reached from the service via `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:sign_completion_verdict`
transition_close.py:169 `return _signing.sign_manifest(ticket_id, manifest, kind="completion-verifier", repo_root=repo_root)` — the caller invokes `sign_manifest`, NOT `mint_opcert_record`
signing.py:595 `return _sign_manifest_under_lock(ticket_id, manifest, kind=kind, repo_root=repo_root)`
signing.py:567 `record = mint_opcert_record(resolved, steps, kind=kind, repo_root=repo_root)` — `_sign_manifest_under_lock` is the sole in-tree caller of `mint_opcert_record`
findings.finding: Step 4's signer-seam patch-site inventory for threading the optional binding parameter is incomplete: the call chain from `sign_completion_verdict` to `mint_opcert_record` passes through two intermediate delegators — `rebar.signing.sign_manifest` (signing.py:587) and `rebar.signing._sign_manifest_under_lock` (signing.py:528) — that the plan never names. `sign_completion_verdict` calls `_signing.sign_manifest(...)` (transition_close.py:169), which delegates to `_sign_manifest_under_lock`, which is the function that actually calls `mint_opcert_record(resolved, steps, kind=kind, repo_root=repo_root)` (signing.py:567). The binding argument cannot reach `mint_opcert_record`/`ensure_opcert_key`/`opcert_principal` without adding it to both delegator signatures, yet the enumeration jumps directly from `sign_completion_verdict` to `mint_opcert_record`.
findings.location: Plan step 4: 'Convert these to accept an explicit signer key handle + principal parameter … the op-cert service passes the startup-bound context-local signer'
scenarios: `rebar.signing.sign_manifest` (signing.py:587) — must accept the optional binding param to forward it; omitted, so the service-supplied signer is dropped at this hop and signing silently falls back to the removed env resolution.

`rebar.signing._sign_manifest_under_lock` (signing.py:528) — the actual caller of `mint_opcert_record`; if its signature is not extended, `mint_opcert_record` can never receive the binding and the seam test (‘sign with a distinct injected key while REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH is unset’) will fail or the code will regress to env reads.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `rebar.signing.sign_manifest` and `rebar.signing._sign_manifest_under_lock` to the list of functions gaining the optional `OpcertSigner`/binding argument; state that `sign_manifest` forwards it to `_sign_manifest_under_lock`, which forwards it to `mint_opcert_record`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the startup-bound signer/principal/push binding crosses the app-owned ThreadPoolExecutor boundary into run_job (explicit copy_context().run wrapper in _offload, or pass the signer as an explicit run_job argument threaded to sign_completion_verdict), since run_in_executor does not propagate contextvars.Context; add a concurrent-worker test that proves the binding is actually visible on the executor thread (not just the default).
evidence: app.py:_offload dispatches run_job via `loop.run_in_executor(app.state.executor, functools.partial(jobs.run_job, ...))` — no context copy

Repo's own gate_context.py:225 documents the requirement: fan-out 'must propagate context via ``contextvars.copy_context().run``'; used at plan_review/generation.py:162 and evals/provider_parity.py:345
run_in_executor does not carry the calling contextvars.Context to the pool thread; a startup-set ContextVar reads its default there

Step 4 already converts ensure_opcert_key/opcert_principal/sign_completion_verdict to accept an EXPLICIT signer argument, which would sidestep the propagation issue if threaded all the way through run_job
findings.finding: The plan asserts the signer/principal/push policy are passed 'context-locally' (contextvars) to jobs and that concurrent/timed-out workers see isolated context, but jobs execute on an app-owned ThreadPoolExecutor via loop.run_in_executor(app.state.executor, functools.partial(jobs.run_job, ...)) in app._offload, which does NOT propagate the caller's contextvars.Context into the worker thread. A ContextVar bound at startup (event-loop/main context) will read its default (unset) inside run_job on the executor thread unless the context is explicitly copied across the hop (contextvars.copy_context().run or an equivalent wrapper) or the signer is passed as an explicit argument. The plan never names this executor->contextvar propagation seam.
findings.location: Plan step 3 ('pass signer/principal/push policy context-locally to jobs'); Testing 'Concurrent/timed-out job tests ... prove context isolation'; AC line 3
scenarios: A gate job runs on the executor thread; the context-local signer reads unset; signing either raises OpcertKeyUnavailable or silently falls back to env/genesis — defeating the cutover
Two concurrent jobs (WORKER_COUNT>1 in a future config) each expect isolated per-context state that was never propagated into their threads
findings.suggested_fix: Since Step 4 already makes the signing functions accept an explicit signer argument, thread the immutable startup signer as an explicit parameter through app._offload -> jobs.run_job -> _dispatch_completion -> sign_completion_verdict rather than relying on a ContextVar across the thread hop; if a ContextVar is retained for principal/push, wrap the executor dispatch with contextvars.copy_context().run (mirroring gate_context.py:225 / generation.py:162) and assert visibility on the worker thread in the concurrency test.
